# Inside the Pḗgasos restoration: what the marks recover
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Pḗgasos** is what the evidence put back.

Pḗgasos is the bridge-figure of Greek myth: born in a monster story, ridden in a hero story, employed in a god story — three genres, one horse. Hesiod tells it in four lines: when Perseus cut the head from Médousa, out sprang great Pḗgasos and the warrior Chrysaōr — her children by Poseidṓn.  The horse flew to the "immortal ones," and Hesiod already knows his office: "he lives in the halls of Zeús, carrying thunder and lightning for the counsellor.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Pḗgasos
- **ASCII form:** pegasos
- **Meaning:** "Possibly from πηγή (spring) or a pre-Greek name"
- **Domain of influence:** Flight, Inspiration, Freedom
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Πήγασος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 190 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Πήγασος**. On the evidence, it means "Possibly from πηγή (spring) or a pre-Greek name".

**Pḗgasos** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *pegasos* and **Pḗgasos** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Pḗgasos** lives at [/sites/pegasos/](/sites/pegasos/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/pegasos/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/pegasos/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/pegasos/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Pḗgasos** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Aviation & Aerospace** — The winged horse; flight’s oldest mascot from Corinth to Mobil’s red Pegasus.
- **Music, Arts & Performance** — Hippocrene: the fountain every poet drinks from.
- **Writing, Publishing & Media** — The Muses’ spring-maker; poetic inspiration in heraldic form.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
